title: Shree Pushkar Chemicals & Fertilisers Ltd - 539334 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Shree Pushkar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 280-281 crore and EBITDA rose 9.7% to Rs 31.9 crore, despite volumes falling sharply.
summary.overview: Revenue grew about 10% YoY on higher realisations even though fertiliser volumes fell to 66,527 MT from 76,288 MT and chemical volumes fell to 9,113 MT from 14,837 MT. EBITDA margin was 11.4% and PAT margin 8.2%, with PAT up about 9% to Rs 22.9 crore. Management said acid plants were run at low load due to high sulphur prices and working-capital strain, and Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 are close to trial operation. Management reiterated an FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, which it said could reach Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, with PAT of around 8.5-9%.

segments.name: Fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 142 crore, up 4% YoY, on 66,527 MT volume (down from 76,288 MT). Management said inventory is being held in anticipation of higher prices.

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Sales value Rs 138 crore, up 17.1% YoY, on 9,113 MT (down from 14,837 MT). Acid plants were put on low load; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover visibility of about Rs 1,250 crore, with management saying it could reach Rs 1,300-1,400 crore (Rs 1,350-1,400 crore in one answer), and PAT of around 8.5-9%.
Management expects Q2 to be better than Q1 and better than Q2 FY26 (about 110% higher, per management's reply to an analyst's Rs 250-285 crore comparison).
Unit 6 expected to start trials by end-August or September 2026, giving about 4-5 months of operation in FY27.
Next year (FY28) with a full 12 months of Unit 6 could reach Rs 1,700-1,750 crore, per management's personal view.
Management says peak revenue for all units could reach about Rs 1,700 crore at current prices once Unit 6 is on stream.
capex_capacity: Cumulative capex of Rs 209 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026 against a total planned Rs 512 crore; about Rs 20 crore spent in Q1 FY27.
Expansions at Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 and Meghnagar are expected to add 450,000 MT per annum of fertiliser capacity and 72,000 MT per annum of chemical capacity.

Unit 5 dyes plant (small vertical, about Rs 37 crore) and 10 MW DC solar project at Nanded are complete or nearing completion; total solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC once commissioned. Capitalisation not yet announced.
Acquired about 30,000 sq m of land adjacent to Unit 1 at Lote Parshuram for Rs 9.3 crore in Q1.
Madhya Bharat (Madhya Pradesh) project has Rs 60 crore invested to June; timeline 2028. Plant is about twice Unit 6 capacity and includes an 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK integration.
Rs 125 crore in non-lien deposits as of 30 June 2026; capex funded from internal accruals and preferential issue proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management says customers are absorbing higher raw material prices, and demand is recovering after a pause during the West Asia conflict.
Sulphur prices have risen to about USD 1,100/t from USD 250-300 earlier, per management; ammonia and sulphur shortages followed Hormuz closure.
K-acid price moved from Rs 550 to Rs 700-plus per management; company says it is the largest K-acid maker in India and has inquiries for K-acid, H-acid and vinyl sulphone from China.
Dye utilisation has decreased due to the global scenario, per management.
Management says it chose value over volume, with dispatches stopped in mid-March 2026 in expectation of higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 volume weakness mitigating, and is the company on track for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is optimistic, citing 40 days of data, and expects Q2 to beat Q1; volumes should be met while protecting value.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 not reflect the upside from orders held back from Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders retracted in Q4 do not carry over into Q1, and that EBITDA and PAT each rose about 10% YoY, so recovery is visible.

qa_highlights.question: Why were acid plants run at low load?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur requires advance payment while acid is sold on credit, and working-capital stress made the margin unattractive; chemical output fell from over 14,000 MT in Q4 to over 9,000 MT in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Should the company fill existing capacity before expanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Unit 5 and 6 are nearly complete and that the Madhya Bharat expansion is also underway, citing confidence in the team and available cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is DAP substitution affecting NPK and SSP demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management questioned DAP availability and said that if DAP is cheaper and available, farmers will shift, so product availability is the key variable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter battery-grade phosphoric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the agenda for now; the focus is on stabilising current expansions first.

risks_watch: Volumes are down about 17% in fertiliser and about 39% in chemicals YoY, and management has prioritised pricing over volume.
Unit 6 start-up timing depends on long-term raw material contracts, due by August or September 2026; ammonia and sulphur supply and price remain volatile with Hormuz still closed.
Working-capital strain from advance sulphur payments; acid plants at low load.
Management guidance has moved between Rs 1,250 crore, Rs 1,300-1,400 crore and Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, and its PAT target is 8.5-9% versus a remark of up to about 10%.
Inconsistent figures in the call: revenue of Rs 280.1 crore vs Rs 281.1 crore; EBITDA of Rs 31.9 crore vs Rs 31 crore; PAT growth of 9.4% vs 9%. Verify against the filing.
Capex of Rs 303 crore remains to be spent against the Rs 512 crore plan.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 280.1 crore (CEO remarks) / Rs 281.1 crore (CFO remarks)
Rs 31.9 crore (11.4% margin); CFO quoted Rs 31 crore

key_quotes: I believe this year will be much better than the last two or three financial years for the company.
So, I believe Q2 will be even better than Q1.
No, sir, you don't expect 10%. I did not say 10%. I said that we will come to the level of 8.5 %- 9%. I hope so.
Honestly speaking, after these sulfur rates came, we put our acid plants on low load.
First, you need value, then volume.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on FY27 outlook and pricing, repeatedly calling the year much better than the last two or three. It was evasive on volume recovery and on the Q4-to-Q1 order-slippage question, answering by pointing to revenue and profit growth instead. It was cautious on Unit 5 and 6 start-up, saying it is taking a measured approach, and it declined to confirm the 10% PAT figure, reiterating 8.5-9%.

adds.what: Ratnagiri Units 5 and 6 fertiliser expansion, with Meghnagar; adds 450,000 MT/yr fertiliser and 72,000 MT/yr chemical capacity
Unit 6 (Ratnagiri) start of trials by end-Aug/Sept 2026, about 4-5 months of operation in FY27
Madhya Bharat (MP) project, about twice Unit 6 capacity, incl. 800 TPD chemical plant for captive NPK
Solar capacity to reach 20.6 MW DC at Nanded (10 MW DC project nearing completion)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 turnover to about Rs 1,250 crore, possibly Rs 1,350-1,400 crore, against roughly Rs 1,030 crore implied by Q1 run-rate, with Unit 6 adding 4-5 months of output; but Q1 volumes fell sharply (fertiliser -13%, chemicals -39%) and acid plants are on low load, so growth is price-led and visibility is uncertain.
